text:
maya: Heads-up — starting a cross-team sync around adding runtime metrics into the console dashboards and the RBAC/sharing model for customer vs internal views. Need inputs from runtime/infra, SRE, product, and security on metric names, cardinality, audit needs, and UX for sharing.

suresh: From runtime side: plan to expose per-route metrics: latency p50/p95, token throughput, inflight queue depth, and error rates. Proposed metric names: `redwood.runtime.route.latency_p50`, `redwood.runtime.route.latency_p95`, `redwood.runtime.route.tokens_per_min`, `redwood.runtime.route.queue_depth`, `redwood.runtime.route.errors`.

suresh: Cardinality we intend: `route_id`, `region`, `model_variant`. Avoid `user_id`/`api_key` in metric labels by default.

maya: Good. SRE/infra — any concerns about cardinality or scrape cost?

eva: SRE: high-cardinality labels will hurt storage and dashboard performance. Please keep the route+region+model_variant constraint for default dashboards. If a team requests customer-scoped metrics, we should serve a pre-aggregated/rolled-up view.

eva: Also suggest sampling for traces/heatmaps, and sample IDs should be redacted for customer-facing previews.

julia: From product: customers want per-route token counts and error rates. For customer-facing dashboards we should surface anonymized model identifiers (e.g., `model-x`), not internal model hashes. Internally we keep full model_version.

catie: Security: any dashboard that can reveal per-customer usage must be gated with RBAC. Minimum requirements: role `customer_view` for shared dashboards, audit log entries when a dashboard is shared (who, when, dashboard_id, included_metrics), and an ability to revoke at the template level.

maya: Proposal for sharing policy: internal dashboards default to org-visible (eng/product/infra). Customer-facing dashboards are created from a template or via a "Create customer view" flow that sets redaction flags and records an audit event.

suresh: Implementation idea: add a telemetry flag `expose_to_customer=true|false` and a transformer step in the metrics pipeline that strips sensitive labels and rewrites model names to anonymized tokens. Example transform config snippet:

```
  transforms:
    - match: "redwood.runtime.route.*"
      redact_labels: ["api_key", "user_id"]
      rewrite_model_name: true
```

catie: We also need retention/audit policies: audit logs retained 1 year, metric aggregates for customer views 30 days by default, internal metrics 90 days. Legal may require longer for compliance — will confirm.

eva: For performance: pre-aggregation is key. Do not allow ad-hoc high-cardinality queries on the customer namespace without approval. Add a cost/estimation UI on the sharing modal so teams know the billing/ingest impact.

julia: UX ask: in modal show exactly which metrics and labels will be included in the shared view and a small preview (scrubbed) so customer support can confirm. Also include an opt-in checkbox for showing cost estimate.

maya: Thoughts on API surfaces? I think separate endpoints make sense: `/api/internal/dashboards` and `/api/customer/dashboards` with different auth scopes and a `?redact=true` param for previews.

suresh: Agreed. We'll add scopes: `dashboards.read.internal`, `dashboards.read.customer`, `dashboards.share`. And we can support `?preview=true` that runs redaction in the pipeline without committing.

maya: Action items from this thread:
- suresh: publish metric name + label spec (including cardinality and optional aggregate keys) by EOD Friday.
- catie: draft audit log schema for share events and retention requirements.
- eva: propose retention & sampling defaults + enforcement points.
- julia: design sharing modal copy + preview mock and include cost estimate placement.
- maya: wire up a short doc + schedule a 30-min sync with security and privacy next Wed.

ops-bot: Created task RDW-1234: "Dashboard metric spec + RBAC sharing policy" assigned to suresh/maya/catie.

suresh: quick note — strongly prefer that we do not add any new tag beyond the planned three (route_id, region, model_variant) to stop cardinality explosion unless we do a cost/impact review.

catie: Also adding a quarterly review requirement for externally shared dashboards to the policy.

maya: Thanks all — I'll collate the notes into the doc and ping folks for the sync. :thumbsup:
